mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) dropping below 3.5% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage inflation and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE is below 3.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during three consecutive months of INDPRO declines exceeding -0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (inflation) above their respective 5-year averages signals a monetary policy shock that combines rate hikes with rising inflation, which historically has been associated with negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 5-year averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) above their 12-month moving averages signals a robust demand recovery, which boosts earnings expectations and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and RSAFS exceed their 12-month averages.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% for four consecutive months, combined with a simultaneous rise in average hourly earnings (not directly available, but implied via labor market tightness), signals wage inflation pressure that erodes margins and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE remains below 4% for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) below its 12-month average for six consecutive months signals a sustained weakness in residential construction demand, which negatively impacts homebuilding and related sectors and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during six consecutive months of HOUST below its 12-month average.
